questions.question: How should you park a motorcycle next to a curb?

options.text: At a 90-degree angle with the rear wheel touching the curb.
At a 45-degree angle with the front tire touching the curb.
Like a car, with the front and rear wheels the same distance from the curb.
At the left edge of the parking space so other drivers can see it better.

questions.correctAnswerText: At a 90-degree angle with the rear wheel touching the curb.
questions.explanation: Park your motorcycle at a 90-degree angle to the curb with your rear wheel touching the curb.

questions.question: What must an eye or face shield do to work properly?

options.text: Prevent all air from passing through.
Not allow eyeglasses to fit underneath.

questions.explanation: An eye or face shield must fasten securely, be free of scratches, resist penetration, allow clear side views, let air pass through to prevent fogging, and allow room for eyeglasses if needed.

questions.question: What should you do when another vehicle passes you from behind?

options.text: Stay in the center portion of the lane.
Stay in the right portion of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in the center portion of the lane.
questions.explanation: When being passed from behind, stay in the center of your lane. Moving closer to the passing vehicle puts you in danger.

questions.question: What does this hand signal mean?
questions.explanation: A left arm bent at the elbow and pointing upward means the rider plans to turn right or change lanes to the right.

questions.question: When should a passenger mount a motorcycle?

options.text: As far back on the seat as possible.

questions.explanation: Passengers should get on a motorcycle only after the engine starts and the transmission is in neutral. They should sit as far forward as possible without blocking the operator's control and hold onto the operator's waist, hips, or belt.

questions.question: How should a group of three-wheel motorcycles travel together?
questions.explanation: Three-wheel motorcycles are too wide for a staggered formation. Groups should travel in a single-file line.

questions.question: What should you do about the oily strip in the middle of the lane?

options.text: Try to avoid it when it is raining.
Ride only on it because it provides better traction.
Avoid the entire center portion of the lane.
Do not worry about oil or other items in the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Try to avoid it when it is raining.
questions.explanation: Oil from cars and trucks builds up in the center of each lane. On dry roads, it usually provides enough traction for motorcycles. The strip is narrow enough that you can ride to either side and still be in the center of the lane.

questions.question: Why should you wear a riding jacket in hot weather?

options.text: It can help protect against heat exhaustion and dehydration.
It is discouraged because it causes heat-related problems.
It should only be done if the jacket is light colored.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can help protect against heat exhaustion and dehydration.
questions.explanation: Wear a riding jacket and long pants in hot weather. They protect you from heat exhaustion and dehydration in addition to other safety benefits.

questions.question: What is true about the center portion of a lane?

options.text: It is always the best part of the lane for a motorcycle.
It often contains oil and grease, but is usually safe for riding.
It often contains oil and grease, and is never safe for riding.
It is the smoothest part of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: It often contains oil and grease, but is usually safe for riding.
questions.explanation: Oil from cars collects in a strip in the center of each lane. On dry roads, this area usually offers enough traction for motorcycles. Avoid large buildups of oil and grease, often found at busy intersections or toll booths.

questions.question: Which part of the lane should you avoid when the road is wet?

options.text: The left portion of the lane.
The center portion of the lane.
The right portion of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The center portion of the lane.
questions.explanation: Oil from cars and trucks collects in the center of each lane. On dry roads, it usually provides enough traction for motorcycles. On wet roads, avoid this strip. It is narrow enough that you can ride to either side and still be in the center of the lane.

questions.question: When someone passes you from behind, what should you do?

options.text: Use the left part of your lane.
Use the center part of your lane.
Use the right part of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the center part of your lane.
questions.explanation: When being passed, stay in the center of your lane. This is the safest position. Riding near the passing vehicle increases crash risk. Riding on the far side may make the other driver return to your lane too soon.

questions.question: When should you increase your following distance?

options.text: When you can see through vehicles in front of you.
When the weather is clear and pleasant.

questions.explanation: Increase your following distance when conditions make stopping harder. This includes heavy traffic, bad weather, night riding, poor visibility of the road ahead, and when you cannot see past the vehicle in front of you.

questions.question: When turning left, what should you do?

options.text: Press both handgrips at the same time.

questions.explanation: A motorcycle leans to turn. Press the handgrip in the direction you want to lean and turn.

questions.question: Most motorcycle crashes happen:

options.text: After riding for a long time.

questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen on short trips less than five miles long at speeds under 30 miles per hour.

questions.question: What should you do when riding in rain or fog?

options.text: Switch between low and high beam settings.

questions.explanation: Use your low beam headlight in rain, snow, or fog. High beams reflect off these conditions and make it harder to see.

questions.question: A rider wearing a helmet is _______ more likely to survive a crash than a rider without a helmet.
questions.explanation: Riders without helmets are three times more likely to die from head injuries in a crash than riders with helmets.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black letters or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They warn drivers about upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: How often should you check a motorcycle's hydraulic fluid at minimum?
questions.explanation: Check hydraulic fluids and coolants at least once a week. Regular inspections before riding help keep you safe.

questions.question: When preparing to pass another vehicle on the left, which part of the lane should you ride in?
questions.explanation: Ride in the left part of your lane when passing on the left. This gives you a better view of the road ahead and makes you more visible to oncoming traffic.

questions.question: How should you apply the front brake?

options.text: Squeeze the lever firmly and smoothly.
Grab the brake with only two fingers.
Press down on the brake lever with your foot.

questions.correctAnswerText: Squeeze the lever firmly and smoothly.
questions.explanation: Squeeze the brake lever with all four fingers. Apply pressure firmly and gradually, increasing force as needed.

questions.question: A rectangular sign can be a:
questions.explanation: Signs that show road rules, like speed limits, are usually rectangular. They are white with black letters or symbols. You must follow the rules shown on these signs.

questions.question: When stopping behind a vehicle, you should:

options.text: Stop far behind the vehicle, then slowly move forward.
Make a quick stop right behind the vehicle.
Stay about four car lengths behind the vehicle.

questions.explanation: Keep a safe distance behind the vehicle in front of you, even when both vehicles are stopped. The vehicle could back up suddenly. You may also need space to move away from a vehicle coming toward you from behind.

questions.question: When stopping, the best way is to:

options.text: Squeeze the front brake lever hard.
Keep your knees against the gas tank and look ahead.
Press the rear brake with increasing pressure.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your knees against the gas tank and look ahead.
questions.explanation: Apply the brakes smoothly and firmly to stop in a straight line. As your motorcycle slows down, gradually use more front brake and less rear brake. Keep your knees against the gas tank and look ahead to stay in a straight line.

questions.question: If you must stop quickly while in a curve, you should:

options.text: Straighten up, square the handlebars, and stop.
Apply both brakes hard while leaning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Straighten up, square the handlebars, and stop.
questions.explanation: If you must stop quickly in a curve, straighten your motorcycle first and square the handlebars, then stop. If you cannot straighten out, apply the brakes smoothly and slowly. Reduce how much you are leaning, then increase brake pressure as you slow down.

questions.question: As the operator, you should tell your passenger to do all of the following, except:

options.text: Get on the motorcycle after the engine has started.
Sit as far forward as possible.
Keep a large space between themselves and you.
Keep their legs away from the muffler and chains.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep a large space between themselves and you.
questions.explanation: Before riding, tell your passenger to get on the motorcycle after you start the engine. They should sit as far forward as they can without crowding you. They should hold onto the passenger handholds or your waist, hips, or belt. They should keep their legs away from the muffler, chains, and moving parts.
